title: Umich 2021 · LocoHub
meta_description: UMich 2021 treadmill walking: what we fixed, what we left out, what we checked and what is still limited.
heading_note: Local review version, not yet released. Nothing on this page has been approved scientifically.
downloads_text: Local review files, not published yet. The full version, the cleaned version, the list of left-out strides and the log of turned ankle samples exist only on the maintainer's computer. They will get download links when they are released.

partly_checked.note: Checked for sudden jumps only; no plausible range exists to check against.

lead: Treadmill walking from {subjects} participants at level, 5° and 10° incline, and 5° and 10° decline, plus the transitions between them (belt speed or slope changing): {recordings} recordings. This is a local review version and is not released. The full version has {full:,} strides; the cleaned version has {filtered:,}. Every stride has exactly 150 samples from 0 to 100 percent of the stride. Joint angles are measured from markers against gravity, power is moment times joint speed, and the pressure point in the foot's frame is published for {legs_published} of {legs_total} legs.

status_words.held: Held back, left as it is

status_key.fixed: A fix was run on real data and a second agent checked it. A fix is not scientific approval.
status_key.left_out: The affected data are left out of the package, with the reason written down. Nothing was shifted or estimated.
status_key.retired: The earlier fix is no longer needed because this version computes the value another way.
status_key.held: The data stay in the package, with the affected columns empty and the reason written down. They were not investigated further.

scope_note: Counts in the grids describe the source recordings each problem touched, measured before the fix for the six earlier problems and in this package for the newer ones. Each card says what this version does about them.
fixed_note: One card per problem. Each card says what was wrong, how much of the data it touched, what we did, how it was checked, and what else it could affect. Example strides were drawn at random with a recorded seed, not hand-picked.

clock.did: We left the six failing recordings out whole instead of shifting or estimating any interval. This is unchanged in this version.
clock.checked: 44 of 50 recordings agree within half a second; the package holds only those 44.
clock.now: In this version none of the six is present.

angle_zero.did: All hip, knee, ankle, thigh, shank and foot angles are computed from markers, as differences of segment angles measured from gravity. Foot angle and its speed are released. Missing markers leave the angle missing; nothing is filled.
angle_zero.checked: A second implementation recomputed 16 legs: no difference.
angle_zero.now: The ankle zero caveat of the earlier version no longer applies.

knee_markers.did: The side-view plane is built with the knee marker KNEM as lateral and KNE as medial.
knee_markers.checked: 14 legs in 7 recordings were checked independently by marker distances: KNEM is lateral in 14 of 14. All 88 legs agree in the build.
knee_markers.now: The reversal is written in the package's list of limitations.

pelvis_backwards.did: For that recording only, the sign of the pelvis tilt was flipped using the marker evidence. This version keeps that pelvis tilt and compares it with the pelvis from markers in every stride.
pelvis_backwards.checked: The published tilt is the mirror of the marker tilt; the flipped tilt overlaps it.
pelvis_backwards.now: Hip angle uses this pelvis, so strides where it disagrees with the marker pelvis by more than 1° have their angle columns left missing.

sign_rule.did: Pelvis tilt is multiplied by −1 in 43 of the 44 recordings (all strides); in AB04 level it is flipped twice, so it ends as published. Hip, knee and ankle are differences of marker angles and keep the direction of their names.
sign_rule.checked: Signs were checked against marker and force-plate evidence in 16 legs.
sign_rule.now: Pelvis tilt keeps the earlier sign step.

thigh_shank.did: Thigh and shank are no longer built from the published pelvis, hip and knee. They are measured from markers in each leg's own plane and released with a foot angle.
thigh_shank.checked: A second implementation recomputed 16 legs: largest difference 0.0 rad.
thigh_shank.now: The earlier formula and its columns are gone.

ankle_180.did: No 180° turn is needed any more. The ankle angle is foot minus shank from markers, so the source's ankle form does not enter. The two strides with one-sample jumps stay left out of both versions.
ankle_180.checked: The 2 jump strides were judged on the source ankle and are not judged again.
ankle_180.now: No stride is turned back in this version.

power.did: Hip, knee and ankle power are now the published moment times our own joint speed: hip is the thigh speed minus the pelvis speed, knee is the thigh speed minus the shank speed (flexion positive), and ankle is the foot speed minus the shank speed. The source's power values are not carried over. Power is missing wherever the moment or a speed is missing. The 1,407 power entries once held back for an unsettled sign are gone, and 174 entries now record power as missing. After the change the gap is zero.
power.checked: A separate readback of every row found power equal to moment times speed to 1e-12 and 29 other columns identical to the earlier version. An independent check of 10 strides drawn with a recorded seed agreed to better than 1e-9 on every row.
power.now: After the change the gap between power and moment times speed is zero.

cop.did: A leg publishes the pressure point only if three checks pass: the ankle moment, held out of the fit, is reproduced (correlation at least 0.95); the toe-off end of the pressure point lies within 4 cm of the toe marker in at least 95% of strides (at 0.2 body weight); and the plate is loaded at the leg's heel strikes in at least 95% of them. Each leg is judged on its own, so a passing leg publishes even when the other leg of the recording is held. 60 of 88 legs pass, and 5,141 strides carry a value. The other 28 legs (2,383 strides) have the three columns present but empty, each with its reason. Published values are labelled 'estimated plate position'.
cop.checked: A second implementation recomputed 16 legs: the unheld pressure point agreed to 7e-16 m and the verdicts were identical. The pass or hold decision of all 88 legs was recomputed from the per-leg numbers: 60 pass, 28 held. Not independent: the plate axis, sign, tilt and shifts were taken from the build's summary.
cop.now: 60 of 88 legs publish the pressure point and 28 are held, each with a reason.

held_back.did: These five recordings are held back and left as they are. The three pressure-point columns are empty, with the reason in each stride's list of empty signals; their angles, moments and power are published like any other recording's. We did not investigate the cause further.
held_back.checked: The pass or hold decision of all 88 legs was recomputed from the per-leg numbers: 60 pass, 28 held, identical to the build's decision.
held_back.now: These recordings stay held back in this version.

limits_intro: Every limitation below stays in the data as a note. Nothing is resampled, filled in or relabelled to hide it. Counts come from the package's own limitations list; a dash means the note has no count of its own.

limit_plain.moments_from_v2: Moments are carried over from the earlier version unchanged. They do not depend on the angles.
limit_plain.power_from_moment_and_speed: Hip, knee and ankle power are the published moment times our own joint speed. The source's power is not carried over.
limit_plain.knee_marker_labels_swapped: The knee marker named KNEM is on the outer side of the knee and KNE on the inner side, the reverse of the usual reading. The evidence is marker positions only.
limit_plain.cop_estimated_plate_position: The pressure point is built on an estimated plate position and passed the checks of its leg. It is not an independently measured foot-frame value.
limit_plain.cop_held_leg: The pressure point is empty because its leg did not pass the checks; the reason is written for each stride.
limit_plain.cop_held_pending_ruling: Five recordings are held back and left as they are: the 10° incline recordings of AB01, AB02 and AB03, AB04 at 10° decline, and AB10 at 5° decline.
limit_plain.angle_columns_missing_in_stride: Some angle columns are missing for a stride because a marker is not visible or the pelvis differs from the pelvis from markers by more than 1°. Nothing is filled.
limit_plain.plane_glitch_hold: One stride has its plane-dependent columns held because the leg plane swung more than 60° from the walking direction.
limit_plain.plate_position_fitted: The force-plate position is not recorded in the source, so it is fitted from the data. It is labelled 'estimated plate position'.

limit_unchecked_intro: Signal families with no limit, so not checked:
limit_unchecked_plain: joint powers (exact moment times speed, but not checked for size)
range of pelvis, thigh, shank and foot angles (jump check only)

exclusion_rows.what: Strides too short or too long to check
exclusion_rows.why: Under 50 or over 250 samples at 100 per second; a stride this short or long cannot be checked against the others.

exclusion_rows.what: Sudden ankle jumps (AB07, 10° incline, right leg)
exclusion_rows.why: Two strides with one-sample ankle jumps, judged on the source ankle. They stay left out and are not judged again.

exclusion_rows.what: Pressure point too far from the foot
exclusion_rows.why: The pressure point is 0.30 to 0.36 m above the foot, mostly late in stance, in 21 strides of 11 legs. Not investigated further.

exclusion_rows.what: Ankle angle outside the possible range (AB04, 5° incline, left leg)
exclusion_rows.why: One stride next to excluded short strides has an ankle angle reaching 85°. Not investigated further.

accounting_note: Accounting: {total} rows. {both} strides are left out of both versions (15 too short or too long, 2 with sudden ankle jumps) and {failed} are left out of the cleaned version only. The full version has {full:,} strides and the cleaned version {filtered:,}, which is the full version minus those {failed}. Six of the 50 treadmill recordings were left out whole before any stride existed (see the timing card), so they are not counted here.

checked: The cleaned version is the full version minus 22 failures and nothing else: every kept stride has identical values in both, every stride has exactly 150 samples from 0 to 100 percent, and every left-out stride has a row and a reason (39 rows). A second agent recomputed this from the files.

Hip, knee and ankle angles against coarse physical limits, all angles for sudden jumps between neighbouring samples, and the pressure point against its distance from the foot. 7,523 of 7,545 strides pass; 22 fail.
Angles, speeds and the pressure point were recomputed by a second implementation on 16 legs: angles and speeds agree to 0.0 rad and the pressure point to 7e-16 m.
Power equals moment times joint speed to 1e-12 in a separate readback of every row, and to 1e-9 in an independent check of 10 strides.
The pressure-point decision (published or held) was recomputed for all 88 legs: 60 published, 28 held, identical to the build.
No angle jump of 30° or more between neighbouring frames in 1,031 stride windows of 12 legs, by a simpler second method.
not_checked: Joint speeds and joint moments have no limit, and power has none either (it is exact moment times speed but not checked for size).
Pelvis, thigh, shank and foot angles were checked for jumps only, not for range.
Belt speeds, and plausible ranges for each task: only coarse limits written before any of these data were read were used. They are not approved reference ranges.

The plate position is fitted, not measured: the pressure point was not compared with a measured foot-frame value, and its axis, sign, tilt and shifts were taken from the build's summary in the independent check.
The knee marker names rest on marker positions only; no photograph or marker-set description was seen.
The two jump strides were judged on the source ankle and not judged again on the ankle from markers.
The cause of the toe-off failure in the held-back 10° incline recordings.
checked.note: A stride that passes has not been shown to be right, only not clearly impossible. A passing check is not scientific approval. Missing samples are never counted as a pass.

phase_note: Mean (line) and spread of one standard deviation (band) of each released signal over the stride, from the cleaned version, for both legs pooled. Colors are the belt speeds (transitions: speeding up or slowing down at two rates). Decline and incline walking pool the 5° and 10° slopes. Power is not in the preview; held pressure points are not in the pressure-point plots. These plots show the data as released; they do not mean the signals are correct.

column_groups.name: Pelvis, thigh, shank and foot angles
column_groups.note: Pelvis from the earlier version, checked against markers; thigh, shank and foot measured from markers against gravity in each leg's side-view plane.

column_groups.name: Hip, knee and ankle angles
column_groups.note: Differences of the segment angles; flexion is positive.

column_groups.name: Angle speeds (pelvis, thigh, shank, foot)
column_groups.note: Slope of the angles over the stride.

column_groups.name: Hip, knee and ankle moments
column_groups.note: Carried over from the earlier version unchanged.

column_groups.name: Pressure point (forward, up, sideways)
column_groups.note: In the ankle frame on an estimated plate position; empty in held legs.

columns_note: Every column has a value for each stride's own leg only; pelvis has no side. There is no time-indexed table, no ground force and no other-leg column in this version.
